transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, I'm pretty sure the people on this environmental modeling contract I'm working on have been tracking my revisions. They've been planting errors in the datasets to make it look like I can't lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes, but... I know what I'm seeing.
How long have you been noticing these supposed errors in the datasets?

It's been about the last two months. That's when I became absolutely certain that the people on this project are tracking my revisions and deliberately planting those errors. Before that, I might have brushed it off, but for the past two months... well, it's just been undeniable to me.
Have you been having any other thoughts that you think might be true, but others around you don't believe?

No, not really. I... I don't think so. It's really just the situation with the modeling contract. I haven't had any other thoughts like that, or anything else going on. It's just the data tampering at work that they refuse to see.
Are you completely sure there are no other situations or things in your life where you think something is happening that others don't believe?

Yes, I'm completely sure. I mean... my life is pretty routine outside of work. I do my job, I come home to my wife. There's nothing else going on. I don't have... suspicions about my neighbors or anything like that, if that's what you mean. 

It is strictly the datasets on this environmental contract. That is the only place where things are happening, because I can see the math changing. But outside of that? No, everything else is completely normal.
Do you think the people tampering with your datasets have a specific motive or goal in mind?

I... well, I don't know exactly what their ultimate goal is. I mean, I can't read their minds. I just know they want to make me look incompetent. 

Maybe they want me off the project so they can bring someone else in, or maybe they're trying to ruin the environmental models for some other reason. I haven't figured out the "why" yet. I just know the "what." The numbers don't add up the way I left them, and that's all the proof I need that they're doing it.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't believe the people on the project were tampering with your datasets?

Well, yes. Before all this started, I didn't have any reason to think that. I'd say... the certainty that people on the project are tracking my revisions and planting these errors, that's been there for about the last two months. Before that, everything seemed fine. But for the past two months, it's been undeniable.
Have your thoughts about the people tampering with your datasets changed at all in intensity or certainty over the past two months?

No, I wouldn't say they've changed. Um... once I saw the pattern about two months ago, I was sure of it. It hasn't really faded or gotten more intense since then. 

It's just... it's just a constant fact now. I log in, I see the math has been altered, and I know they did it. So, my certainty has stayed pretty much exactly the same the whole time.
Have you ever had a similar feeling of certainty about something being true that others didn't believe, outside of this work project?

No, not really. I mean... I've always just focused on my work, the numbers. The math is the math, you know? I haven't had anything else like this happen where people didn't believe me about something I knew was a fact. It's just this situation with the datasets.
Have you ever felt like you're being watched or followed, even when you're alone or there's no one around?

No, I can't say that I have. Um... I don't feel like anyone is physically following me down the street or watching me in my house, if that's what you mean. 

It's really just the digital side of things—them tracking my revisions on the project and altering the numbers. But physically being watched? No. When I'm alone, I'm just alone.
Have you ever had any other situations in your life where you felt someone was out to get you or hurt you in some way?

No, I haven't. Um... I've never really had any problems with people trying to hurt me or, you know, being out to get me. 

I've always just kept my head down and done my work. This whole thing with the datasets is... well, it's really the only time something like this has happened. Before this, nobody's ever tried to sabotage me or anything like that. So, no, nothing else comes to mind.
Do you think you will ever change your mind about the people tampering with your datasets?

Change my mind? No, I don't see how I could. I mean, that's really the whole reason I'm here. 

I am pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions. They're planting errors in the datasets to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. My wife keeps trying to tell me it's just version-control mistakes. The junior analysts say the exact same thing... that it's just a versioning error in the system. 

But I've been doing this a long time. I know what I calculated and I know what I entered. So, no, I'm not going to change my mind when I can see exactly what they're doing to my files.
Have you ever thought that there might be other people, outside of this project, who are against you or trying to harm you in some way?

No, no one else. Um... like I was saying earlier, I've never really had issues with people being out to get me before this. 

It's strictly the people on this specific contract. I don't have any reason to think anyone outside of work even cares about what I'm doing, let alone wants to harm me. It's just about the data and... well, them wanting me off the project. Outside of that, everything in my life is completely normal. So, no, definitely no one else.
Have you ever had any moments where you doubted that the people on the project were tampering with your datasets?

No, I haven't. Um... like I said just a minute ago, that's exactly why I'm here. I haven't doubted it because I'm pretty sure—well, I know for a fact—that the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions. 

They are planting those errors in the datasets specifically to make it look like I can't lead the work. So even when my wife or the junior analysts try to tell me it's just version-control mistakes... no, I don't doubt it at all. I know what's happening.
Has your conviction about the data tampering changed at all since you first became certain of it two months ago?

No, it hasn't changed at all. I know I sound like a broken record here, but that is exactly why I'm sitting in this room. 

I am just as sure now as I was two months ago that the people on that environmental modeling contract are tracking my revisions. They are still planting errors in the datasets to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. My wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes, but... well, they're wrong. I know what I'm looking at. So no, my certainty hasn't changed one bit.
Do you think it's possible that you might be mistaken about the people tampering with your datasets?

No, I really don't think I'm mistaken. I mean, I know we keep going over this, but I'm looking right at the data. I can see where they've been tracking my revisions on the environmental modeling contract. They are planting those errors in the datasets, clear as day. It's all just to make it look like I'm incompetent and can't lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts... they keep trying to tell me it's just version-control mistakes, but I know what I'm seeing. So, no, I don't think it's possible I'm mistaken.
Have you considered the possibility that the errors in the datasets could be due to your own mistake?

No, I haven't. I... I've been doing this kind of mathematical and data work for a long time, so I know what my own work looks like. It's not my mistake. 

The people on that environmental modeling contract are tracking my revisions and putting those errors in the datasets on purpose. They just want it to look like I can't lead the work anymore. I know my wife and the junior analysts keep saying I probably just messed up the version control, but... no. I know what I'm doing, and I know it's not me making these mistakes.
Have you ever had any other thoughts or beliefs that you were absolutely certain of, but which others did not believe, outside of your work or personal relationships?

No, not really. I mean, outside of what's happening at work with the datasets, I haven't had anything like that. I'm a pretty logical guy, you know? I deal with facts and numbers. So, no, I haven't had any other beliefs that people told me were wrong... just this situation with the modeling contract.
Has your belief that the people on the project are tampering with your datasets ever wavered, even for a moment?

No, it hasn't wavered. Not even for a second. I mean, that's why I'm here talking to you, honestly. I'm pretty sure... well, I *know* the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and planting those errors in the datasets. They want to make it look like I can't lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes, but I know what I'm looking at. So no, I haven't doubted it.
Have you developed a detailed theory or explanation for why the people on the project are tampering with your datasets?

Well, no, not really. I mean... I don't have some big, complicated theory about it. 

Like I said, they just want it to look like I can't handle leading the work anymore. I don't know if one of them wants my position or if they just don't like how I run things... I haven't really spent time trying to figure out their exact motives. I'm a numbers guy, so I just deal with the facts in front of me. And the fact is, the files are being altered. I don't really need a detailed explanation to see what's happening right there on the screen.
